name: claude-market-private
description: Private Claude Code plugin marketplace for ozzycodes2.

plugins.name: review
plugins.description: Comprehensive multi-phase PR review — change analysis, 3-pass deep code review, security scanning, test analysis, and documentation-drift checks, posted as one unified GitHub review. Plus monitor-pr: continuously watch a PR for CI failures and review comments (drive with /loop), fix them via subagents in parallel, and resolve or reply-acknowledge each comment once its fix ships. Rust and Machinify mac-ui changes get tailored checks.

plugins.name: session-improv
plugins.description: Query Claude Code session history and conversation data with SQL (DuckDB) via cc-query. Provides the reflect skill for session analysis, token usage, tool patterns, and agent activity.

plugins.name: agent-authoring
plugins.description: Author and improve agent-facing instructions and skills. Restructures bloated CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md via progressive disclosure and converts deterministic CLI-policy rules into enforced PreToolUse hooks (agent-docs-improv), and gives guidance for writing effective skills and agent docs (writing-for-agents).

plugins.name: architecture-design
plugins.description: Design deep modules and sharpen a project's domain model. Shared vocabulary for module depth, interfaces, and seams; domain terminology, ADRs, and CONTEXT docs; and a codebase deepening scan with an HTML report. Run setup-matt-pocock-skills once first.

plugins.name: grilling
plugins.description: Relentless interviews to stress-test a plan, decision, or design before you commit to it. Provides grilling (the core interview), grill-me (a quick trigger), grill-with-docs (grilling that also produces ADRs and a glossary as decisions crystallize), and wayfinder (plan work too large for one session as a map of decision tickets, resolved one at a time).

plugins.name: session-mgmt
plugins.description: Manage the full lifecycle of a Claude Code working session. start-session opens a task in a fresh, isolated git worktree (via EnterWorktree, never `git worktree add`) named after the argument, and loads the JIRA story when the name is an issue key. exit-session detects and tears down the ephemeral resources a session created — background processes, Docker/compose stacks, local Kubernetes, git worktrees, throwaway local branches, and temp files — with a plan-confirm-execute flow that never destroys data without confirmation.
